text:
Anya Kapoor: FYI saw a surge of 429s for a handful of Hosted customers starting ~15:02 UTC after the limiter rollout. error rate ~3.4% for 10m, latency increased. tagging @Charlie (oncall) and @Darren for triage
Charlie (oncall): on it. pulling limiter metrics and recent deploys. which shard/region?
Anya Kapoor: US-west-2 primary. looks like affected customers are on hosted-pool-3. Support tickets opened by Maria.
Maria Santos: Customer-facing: multiple customers reported timeouts and 429s, some escalated to billing because retries spiked token usage. I've paused retries on their SDK side and notified them we have an internal ticket.
Darren Lee: I see the deploy: limiter v2.14 rolled at 15:00 UTC. Quick diff shows we changed the burst-keying from customer_id -> global_bucket for a performance experiment. suspect that change allowed cross-customer bursting into shared capacity.
Kevin Park: that matches the spike shape — global bucket gives high short-term throughput then exhausted shared pool, resulting in head-of-line blocking and 429/503 for others.
Charlie (oncall): Rolling back limiter v2.14 on hosted pools now. initiating canary rollback to pool-1.
sre-bot: deploy rollback started for service=limiter hostgroup=hosted-pool-3 user=charlie
Darren Lee: we should also scale the hosted-pool-3 by +2 GPUs temporarily while rollback finishes, to absorb any remaining backlog.
Anya Kapoor: scaling requested. also patching routing fallback to prefer dedicated-pool when available for committed customers to avoid billing impacts.
Kevin Park: quick repro steps for postmortem / QA:
1) set limiter config keying to `global_bucket` in test cluster
2) run 500 concurrent short requests from 20 distinct tenant ids with bursty inter-arrival
3) watch `tokens_available` metric and per-tenant `throttle_count`
Command I used:
```
# reproduce burst exhaustion
ab -n 2000 -c 500 -H "Authorization: Bearer tenant-123" https://test-hosted/api/v1/generate
```
Metrics query:
```
sum(rate(limiter_throttle_total[1m])) by (tenant_id)
sum(limiter_tokens_available) by (bucket)
```
Darren Lee: here's the faulty config snippet (from v2.14):
```yaml
limiter:
  buckets:
    - name: shared-global
      key: global_bucket   # <-- incorrectly set, should be tenant_id
      capacity: 10000
      refill_rate: 5000
```
Correct config should use `tenant_id` or `customer_id` as key.
Maria Santos: support notes: customers A, B, C filed tickets (IDs: SUP-8943, SUP-8947, SUP-8950). Maria -> already informed them of rollback and temporary compensatory credits. they want timeline and mitigation plan.
Charlie (oncall): rollback finished 15:18 UTC, error rate dropped to baseline by 15:26. scaling down the extra capacity now.
sre-bot: deploy rollback completed for service=limiter hostgroup=hosted-pool-3 status=success
Darren Lee: root cause: an experiment merged a change to the limiter keying that wasn't gated by canary or feature flag. it turned many per-tenant token buckets into one global bucket.
Kevin Park: immediate mitigations applied:
- rollback v2.14 across hosted pools (completed)
- temporarily scaled hosted-pool-3 +2 GPUs during rollback
- updated routing to prefer dedicated capacity for reserved customers
- paused SDK auto-retries for impacted customers (coord with support)
Longer-term actions (owner tags):
- (Darren) add automatic gating: limiter keying changes must be behind a feature flag scoped to a single canary hostgroup
- (Kevin) add unit/integration tests that simulate multi-tenant burst scenarios in CI (test harness + synthetic tenants)
- (Anya) add alert: sudden drop in per-tenant variance + spike in global throttle rate => auto-create incident and page oncall
- (Maria) update support runbook and customer communication template for limiter incidents
- (Charlie) postmortem and timeline doc within 48h
Anya Kapoor: proposed monitoring tweak: emit `limiter_bucket_key_mode{mode="per-tenant"|"global"}` and enforce an aggregator alert if it flips outside of expected for production.
Darren Lee: quick patch landing reference (PR-4521). Patch will validate config on deploy: ensure no production hostgroup has `key: global_bucket` unless opt-in label present.
Kevin Park: also adding a safety: max-burst-per-tenant cap that can't be exceeded even in global mode, as an extra guard.
Maria Santos: preparing customer comms draft, will attach timeline and mitigation.
Charlie (oncall): closing immediate incident. will monitor dashboards for 24h. please ack here when your action items are done so I can close the incident ticket. :white_check_mark:
Anya Kapoor: ack, will own the alert and telemetry change.
Darren Lee: ack, will file PR and add gating.
Kevin Park: ack, starting CI tests and safety cap implementation.
Maria Santos: ack, customer comms in progress.
support-bot: incident INC-2026 created, severity=high, assignees=[Anya Kapoor, Darren Lee, Kevin Park, Maria Santos, Charlie (oncall)]
Anya Kapoor: quick note for post-incident doc: include repro artifacts (ab command, PromQL queries), config diff, timeline, and customer impact table (requests, throttles, cost impact). we should also schedule a 1hr blameless review with product and devex to discuss safe experiments.
Charlie (oncall): leaving this thread open until postmortem is published. thanks everyone for quick response. :heart:
